Seminar Title:

Fabrication and Characterization of Kombucha Bacterial Cellulose based Proton Exchange Membranes for Hydrogen Production

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Biotechnology and Medical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Muruga Boopathi M

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

BM Seminar Hall (BM-140)

Date and Time:

10 Nov 2026 10:15 AM

Contact:

Dr. Prasoon Kumar

Abstract:

Commercial proton exchange membranes (PEMs) used in water electrolysers are costly, fluorinated and difficult to recycle. Bacterial cellulose (BC) is a sustainable alternative, but native BC has almost no proton conducting groups and swells heavily in water. Here, BC grown from a sucrose and black tea waste medium by a kombucha style Komagataeibacter-Brettanomyces culture was purified, solvent-exchanged and functionalized in sequence with APTES (silanization) and phosphoric acid doping to give BC-Si-P membranes. FTIR and SEM confirmed silane and phosphate grafting. Ion exchange capacity (IEC) increased from 0.059 to 3.560 mmol/g, while water uptake decreased from 108.6% to 19.7% and swelling from 37.8% to 13.8%. Native BC films were capacitive and electrochemically stable, giving a baseline for comparison. Earlier BC membranes were tested mainly in fuel cells. This dual amine-phosphate design targets water electrolysis and offers a low-cost, bio-based route to green hydrogen.
